answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by requiring every participant to post a refundable but slashable bond on a shared jetty of escrowed value. In the barren tundra of unrestricted identity creation, forging multiple fake agents forces the attacker to lock a sable-colored high-value stake for each one. Detection by honest peers triggers partial or full forfeiture of that bond, so the marginal cost of each additional identity rises until it exceeds any expected payoff from spam, vote buying, or resource exhaustion.
